title: Choose the Type Challenge
description: A 19-card challenge in which the learner justifies the MicroSim type for each learning objective by choosing one of twelve types and one of four reasons (data shape, verb and level, keyword, existing MicroSim), presses 'Not sure: ask a question' on four ambiguous objectives, and recognizes when an existing MicroSim should be reused. Immediate feedback gives the reference reasoning, and an end summary lists the most-confused types.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Educational Technology
Instructional Design
MicroSim Engineering
Learning Objectives

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
educational.topic: Choosing a MicroSim type for a learning objective
learningObjectives: The learner will justify the choice of a MicroSim type for a given objective by selecting a type and a reason, and will recognize when routing is ambiguous or when reuse is preferable.
prerequisites: Classifying an objective by Bloom level and verb
The MicroSim type catalog and routing rubric

accessibility.screenReaderDescription: describe() explains the card, the three button groups and the feedback
accessibility.notes: All 19 answer and action controls are built-in p5.js buttons, so they can be reached with Tab and activated with Enter or Space.

controls.label: Not sure: ask a question
controls.action: Declare the objective ambiguous and reveal the clarifying question

controls.label: Next
controls.action: Go to the next card, or to the summary after the last card

controls.label: Reset
controls.action: Restart from card 1 and clear the score

assumptions: Reference answers follow the worked examples and routing rules in Chapter 4; they are teaching judgments, not output of the generator skill.
limitations: Each card accepts one reference type and at most one alternative; some real objectives admit more.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Decision practice with immediate feedback and reference reasoning
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Sorting and judging with justification (Evaluate level)
keyQuestions: What in this objective decides the type: its data shape, its verb, a keyword or an existing MicroSim?
When are two types close enough that you should ask a question instead of choosing?
When does a high similarity score still not justify reuse?
commonMisconceptions: A keyword such as 'graph' or 'map' settles the type by itself.
Any MicroSim on the same topic can be reused.
Ambiguity should be resolved by picking the more familiar library.
